profile_likelihood.cell: A_31, high- to low-volatility state (sigma-ascending labels)
profile_likelihood.method: Profile log-likelihood l_p(a) = max over all other parameters of logL subject to A_31 = a, computed by constrained EM: the E-step is unchanged and the M-step sets A_31 = a and A_3k proportional to the expected transition counts out of state 3 for k = 2, 3 (the exact maximiser of the expected complete-data log-likelihood under the constraint). Each constrained run starts at the unconstrained maximum and stops at |dlogL| < 1e-10. LR(a) = 2 (l_max - l_p(a)). The maximum lies on the boundary, a_hat = 0, so only an upper bound is informative. The 95% upper bound is the a at which LR(a) = 2.706: the signed-root LR statistic is asymptotically standard normal for an interior true value, so a one-sided 95% bound uses z_0.95^2 = 2.706, and at a true value on the boundary the LR statistic is a 50:50 mixture of chi2_0 and chi2_1 (Chernoff 1954; Self and Liang 1987), whose 95% quantile is also 2.706. The chi2_1 crossing at 3.841 is the upper end of the two-sided 95% interval, equivalently a one-sided 97.5% bound, and is reported as the conservative figure.

boundary.note: score ratio G_31 / n_3 at the maximum with A_31 held at zero; below one the unconstrained maximum is on the boundary

rule_of_three_same_sample.note: 3/n treats the latent high-state hours as observed Bernoulli trials; it is not a likelihood-based bound for a hidden chain

multistart_at_bound.note: constrained EM at A_31 = bound from the 8 starts of the paper's K=3 fit (seed 45) and the 40 starts of its model-selection fit (seed 48), the cell held between each start's highest- and lowest-sigma states, tolerance 1e-9. Starts whose converged states are no longer in sigma-ascending order have held a different cell (in practice low-to-high) and are excluded; a gain above zero among the rest would mean the profile started at the MLE is only local

calibration_at_bound.design: paths of T = 3,507 hours simulated from the constrained fit at A_31 = bound (stationary start); on each, the LR statistic for A_31 = bound with a_hat from the boundary decision and the converged unconstrained EM; the one-sided test rejects when a_hat < bound and LR >= 2.706

calibrated.method: Parametric-bootstrap test inversion. At each a, paths of T = 3,507 hours are simulated from the constrained maximum-likelihood fit with A_31 = a; on each the one-sided statistic (LR for A_31 = a when a_hat < a, else 0) is computed as in calibration_at_bound. The p-value of a is the share of simulated statistics at least as large as the observed LR(a); the 95% bound is the a at which the p-value falls to 0.05, linear in a between grid points.
calibrated.note: Both bounds use the Gaussian HMM likelihood, and the chi2 calibration of the profile block assumes that model as well, which the residual diagnostics reject. Within the model the chi2 bound is conservative: its simulated size at the bound is profile_likelihood.calibration_at_bound.rejection_rate, against a nominal 5%. The bootstrap inversion here rejects every A_31 > 0 on the grid, because LR(a) rises almost linearly from zero, so the p-value of a small a is close to the probability that a path simulated from the fitted HMM has a score ratio at zero as low as the observed one, and the observed ratio (profile_likelihood.boundary.score_ratio_at_zero) lies in the lower tail of the ratios simulated under the fitted HMM (power.sub_period.*.score_ratio). That is a misspecification signal, not a bound: upper_bound_bootstrap_95 is then null. Among three-state fits to GARCH(1,1) paths the observed ratio is typical of the conventional Student-t GARCH and within the range of the fitted one (garch_generic.*.share_paths_ratio_at_most_observed).

garch_generic.design: Paths of T = 3,507 hourly returns simulated from single-regime GARCH(1,1) processes, the variance recursion started at the sample variance of the sub-period returns (the backcast of diagnostics.fit_garch11). A K=3 Gaussian HMM is fitted to each path with the paper's protocol (8 random starts, seeded per path), once capped at 150 iterations as the paper's fits were and once run to tol 1e-6 (cap 20,000); for the converged fit the boundary decision of the power block says whether the maximum-likelihood A_31 is exactly zero (share_mle_zero: at the best of the 8 starts). The 8-start optimum can be a local one, so the paths named in wide_paths_per_specification are also fitted from 24 further starts with volatilities spread log-uniformly over 0.15-3.5 x the path's s.d. (hmm_batch.spread_starts) and the decision is repeated at the best optimum over all 32 starts (wide_multistart; per path under paths[*].wide). For the Gaussian GARCH that is every path, and its zero share is wide_multistart.share_mle_zero_best_optimum; for the Student-t specifications it is a check on the first 30 paths. Every specification draws its path seeds from the same sequence, so the first 60 paths share seeds across specifications. A GARCH(1,1) variance can fall by at most the factor beta per hour; the zero share follows beta (largest_hourly_variance_fall_factor_beta) more closely than persistence. In these fits the high state is rarer and more extreme than in the data's (median_ann_sigma_pct, median_high_state_mass).

spec.source: alpha 0.10, beta 0.88, nu 4, omega matching the sample variance of the sub-period returns

garch_generic.data_for_reference: the sub-period fit has A_31 on the boundary (profile block); observed_score_ratio_at_zero is its score ratio

convergence.protocol: GaussianHMM.fit, as now shipped (regime_engine.hmm_batch.fit_protocol): every random start (the same seeds and starting points as before) runs Baum-Welch until the log-likelihood rises by less than 1e-6, with a safeguard cap of 100,000 iterations; the first start with the largest final log-likelihood is selected and continued until |dlogL| < 1e-9 and no parameter moves by more than 1e-10 per iteration (means and volatilities in units of the state's volatility, transition probabilities as they are). 'capped' is the same run read off at the cap of the earlier artifacts (150 iterations, 300 for model selection) with the selection made there; it reproduces the numbers printed in version 1.2.0 of the paper (8 October 2026); 'where' gives their place in that version. 'tol_only' is the selected start where the 1e-6 rule left it, before the polish. Information criteria are evaluated at the returned parameters.

convergence.full_sample_note: The full-sample K=3 fit (T = 5,001; Table 7, Figure 8) used a 150-iteration cap, but its hourly returns are no longer available, so it cannot be refitted and whether it converged cannot be checked. On the sub-period the same cap left the log-likelihood 9.8e-05 below the converged value and moved no annualised volatility by more than 0.040 points (sub_period_cap_effect).

power.design: Paths simulated from the K=3 Gaussian HMM with the high-to-low cell set to each alternative (mass moved from the high-to-moderate cell, as in diagnostics.boundary_power), starting from the stationary distribution. share_mle_zero: the likelihood is maximised with A_31 held at zero, starting from the data-generating parameters (tol 1e-7 on |dlogL|), and the score ratio G_31 / n_3 is evaluated there; the maximum-likelihood estimate of A_31 is exactly zero when the ratio is at most one. This is the estimator at convergence; it does not depend on how fast EM approaches the boundary.

parameters.full_sample: output/summary_FULLSAMPLE_2025-10-02_to_2026-04-28.json, kernel reconstructed by diagnostics.reconstruct_transition_matrix, T = 5,001; seeds as diagnostics.boundary_power (base 20260820 + int(a * 1e6)), so the first 200 paths at 0.003 and 0.01 are those behind output/bootstrap_hmm.json
parameters.sub_period: output/summary.json return_K3, T = 3,507; seeds base 20261820 + int(a * 1e6)

power_em.design: The first paths of each cell of the power block. (1) The published rule: Baum-Welch from the data-generating parameters with the stopping rule of GaussianHMM.fit, tol 1e-6, cap 400, A_31 < 1e-8 counted as zero -- the procedure behind output/bootstrap_hmm.json boundary_power_full_sample. (2) The same EM continued to |dlogL| < 1e-10, cap 2,000. (3) The maximum-likelihood estimate: the boundary decision at the converged fit and, where the estimate is interior, EM restarted from the constrained maximum with A_31 = 1e-3 (EM cannot leave an exact zero, so at a true A_31 = 0 the rules (1) and (2) return zero on every path by construction). EM approaches a boundary maximum geometrically at the rate of the score ratio, so (1) and (2) undercount zeros whenever the ratio is close to one.
